system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Power: AI, Energy Wars, and Market Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is in dynamic flux as technological rivalry (AI, chips, and platform control), energy supply conflicts (Iran, Venezuela, Hormuz disruptions) and a stressed financial system (bond-market selloffs, rising yields) interact to reshape state and corporate behaviour. States use transactional diplomacy and commercial leverage while non-state tech actors and markets amplify shocks; regional wars and domestic politics (far-right gains, protests) increase fragmentation and accelerate strategic decoupling. These interacting processes produce feedbacks across capital flows, supply chains and security postures that make the system more brittle and unpredictable.
system_description.scope: Major state actors and alliances, transnational markets (energy, finance, commodities), multinational corporations and tech labs, international institutions, supply chains (chips, rare earths, shipping), information and cyber operations, and the flows of capital, energy, and data that connect them.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-economic-ecological system (the wider global human-environment system that constrains resources, climate risk and long-term economic carrying capacity).
adjacent_subsystems: Global Financial & Monetary System (bond markets, FX, sovereign wealth funds)

variables.name: US–Iran maritime and military escalation
variables.description: Direct military and maritime clashes between the United States and Iran — including strikes on tankers and engagements with naval vessels — are intensifying and shifting regional deterrence dynamics and crisis management calculus.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and diplomatic contest
variables.description: The sustained war between Russia and Ukraine, marked by drone and missile strikes, battlefield attrition and intermittent peace-talk initiatives involving outside mediators, is reshaping military balances and European security arrangements.

variables.name: Global energy supply and price shocks
variables.description: Tightening oil and gas markets driven by production choices, sanctions, refinery outages and logistical chokepoints are elevating prices, shifting producer–consumer leverage and forcing new energy-security responses across markets.

variables.name: Strategic tech and AI competition
variables.description: An intensifying contest over semiconductors, AI models and data governance among major states and leading firms — led by rival blocs centered on the United States and China — is redirecting investment, trade barriers and global standards-setting.

variables.name: Global financial and monetary reconfiguration
variables.description: A broad repricing of risk — driven by rising bond yields, central bank policy divergence and large sovereign fund and institutional portfolio moves — is reordering capital flows and weakening prior assumptions of the post‑2008 monetary equilibrium.
